page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.16xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized server powered by an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. It features 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The memory configuration consists of 128.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of memory per core. The instance utilizes the Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 12 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight strong memory read performance, with small block cached reads reaching 4612.53 GB/sec and large block uncached reads at 200.81 GB/sec. The processor demonstrates strong capabilities in specialized tasks, scoring 67458.21 on the PassMark CPU test and showing high performance in extended instructions, encryption, and physics simulations. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 314.73 GB/sec, and software compilation via Clang scored 43620.0. In database and key-value operations, the server achieved 69.84 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks and strong PassMark database operation metrics.

Given its compute-heavy profile and lack of local storage, this instance is highly suited for network-dependent, compute-intensive workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, and cryptography. It also supports moderate LLM inference, demonstrating strong prompt processing speeds for small and medium models. The flex designation indicates a resource-dense, cost-efficient compute option for workloads that benefit from high-frequency Intel Xeon processors and DDR5 memory without requiring local NVMe storage.
